gaps.lead: She got up early so that she wouldn't miss the train.
gaps.sentence: She got up early ___ the train.
gaps.explanation: so as not to / in order not to + infinitive express negative purpose.

gaps.lead: Both sisters play the violin beautifully.
gaps.sentence: The sisters ___ play the violin beautifully.
gaps.explanation: Both (the) sisters… / The sisters both… — with the given frame, 'both' precedes the verb.

gaps.lead: 'I broke the window,' said the boy.
gaps.explanation: admit + -ing (optionally 'to'): admitted breaking / admitted to breaking.

gaps.lead: It was unfair of the referee to send him off.
gaps.explanation: shouldn't have + participle criticises a past action.

gaps.lead: 'I've never been to Asia,' she told me.
gaps.sentence: She told me that ___ to Asia.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect shifts to past perfect: she had never been.

gaps.lead: I don't usually drink coffee at night.
gaps.explanation: be (not) used to = (not) accustomed to: I'm not used to coffee at night.
